I will keep to the wheat-maize rotation this year, because that is the most reliable way for me to use the land in Quzhou County and spread my risk across the full year. At the start of the growing season, I will carry my winter wheat through to harvest, then I will sow summer maize right after, because this rotation matches my local climate, my labor capacity, and the need for steady grain output rather than chasing a risky cash crop. I will use improved seed for wheat and hybrid seed for maize, because I want stable yields and better resistance without making the management too complicated. I will keep fertilizer at moderate levels, use a few timely irrigations when the crop most needs water, and spray only as needed to control the main diseases and insects. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage before maize after wheat harvest, because it is faster and easier for me to manage than deep ploughing every season. My goal is not the highest possible yield, but a dependable harvest with work I can realistically handle.
